ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the upper left of the figure is an LM7806 three-terminal voltage regulator; pin 1 IN is connected to the input Ui, pin 3 OUT is connected to the output terminal Uo on the right, and pin 2 GND is connected to the lower control node. On the right there is R4=2 kΩ and the voltage regulator diode VZ forming a 5 V reference node, and this node is connected to the non-inverting input of the op amp. Around the op amp, R2=4 kΩ and R3=2 kΩ can be seen forming a feedback voltage divider network, and the op amp output is used to adjust the GND pin potential of the LM7806; the output terminal of the LM7806 is the load output Uo. Reasoning: According to the connection in the figure, the op amp and R2, R3 form a non-inverting amplification relation for the 5 V voltage-regulated reference, so the GND pin voltage of the LM7806 is Vg=(1+R2/R3)·Vz=(1+4 kΩ/2 kΩ)×5 V=15 V. The LM7806 maintains about 6 V between its OUT and GND pins, that is, Uo−Vg=6 V. Therefore Uo=15 V+6 V=21 V.

method.method_draft: First describe the visual circuit nodes: the Zener clamps its node to 5 V, and by the op-amp feedback the R2/R3 junction must also be 5 V. Since the op-amp input draws negligible current, the current through R3 is I=5 V/2 kΩ=2.5 mA, and the same current flows through R2=4 kΩ. Therefore the voltage drop across R2 is 2.5 mA*4 kΩ=10 V, putting the LM7806 GND pin node at 5+10=15 V relative to the bottom rail. Finally add the LM7806 regulated 6 V between OUT and GND pin: Uo=15+6=21 V.
